tasks.analysis: Mass extinctions have periodically reshaped the diversity of life on Earth, representing significant biological and ecological shifts. The most famous event, the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction, occurred approximately 66 million years ago and led to the demise of the dinosaurs. Large-scale losses of species are often caused by catastrophic events such as volcanic eruptions, asteroid impacts, and climate change. The resulting damage to biodiversity disrupts ecosystems and alters evolutionary trajectories.
